We enhance a result by Freiman from 2004, showing that the distance between any integer subset A of a real subset of the reals and a subset with a structure similar to an arithmetic progression is at most one, where subsets A with a small sum set will conform to this improved standard.

Given any Brownian motion $B$ and a positive real number $a$, our study examines the image of the function generated by fractional Brownian motion with a fixed positive drift, denoted as $m \mapsto f(m,B)(m)$, where $f(m,x)=x+m^{a}$. When the Hurst parameter $H$ is less than $1-\frac{1}{a}$, we discover that the image has a non-empty interior, consisting of disjoint intervals. However, for values of $H$ greater than or equal to $1-\frac{1}{a}$, the image has positive Lebesgue measure. Notably, these findings relate to the question of whether the image has a non-empty interior for all values of $H$ in the interval $(0,1)$.

This study explores the impact of quantum disorder on the classic Henon-Heiles model, 
utilizing Dirac's time-independent variational principle and the H-K method by Jackiw and Kerman. 
Our approach yields results that closely mirror those obtained through numerical solutions 
of the H-K equation via the Adiabatic Approximation (Born-Oppenheimer) and direct 
integration, particularly for higher-energy states. 
As quantum disorder rises, 
significant deviations from classical predictions emerge, 
resulting in hysteresis and non-convergent variations in ground-state energy with shifting parameters. 
These findings are confirmed by computational simulations and exhibit convergence with varying quantum disorder.

We introduce a potential task involving predicting ICU admission for COVID-19 patients based on medical X-ray images, as official data for training predictive models is limited. Initially, we gathered 4375 CT scans from various sources and tailored the images to a consistent format, resulting in a dataset with 1924 images labeled positive or negative for COVID-19. Although this dataset isn't ideal for predicting ICU admissions, it enabled us to develop and test three models using publicly available datasets that do include such information, namely COVID-NA, COVID-MAR19, and COVID-MARS19. We found that features visible in medical imaging can signify severe disease progression, and thus have potential value in informing ICU readiness.

We've already established that the universal simplicial collection possesses a group structure at each level of n. Our objective is to demonstrate that this collection has a group structure that persists across all its simplicial components.

Despite significant advancements, Visual Relationship Detection (VRD) still struggles with precision issues, as many predicted relationships don't match the actual targets and may mislead downstream tasks such as scene graph generation and visual navigation. This problem stems from limited data, making it difficult for models to accurately identify object boundaries, locate objects and discern relationships between them. To address this, the current study focuses on filtering out incorrect predictions, assuming the model's understanding of objects is generally reliable. During the data preparation phase, we propose an innovative strategy to eliminate low-confidence VRD predictions, allowing the model to concentrate on confirming the validity of remaining candidates, which starts with simple classification and is made more complex by the arrangement of remaining objects. To demonstrate, we experiment with two prominent VRD benchmarks, establishing a filtered dataset that requires 50% fewer correct predictions to achieve the same performance levels as the original. However, our results show a substantial 12% improvement in accuracy compared to the baseline, as opposed to a mere 2% improvement with traditional filtering methods.

This study introduces an innovative action recognition framework that utilizes deep learning techniques. To improve the model's efficiency and adaptability, particularly in low-light conditions, a specialized variant of BERT called R-BERT is developed. The unique training approach of R-BERT involves using "full" and "delta" samples, which allows the variant to share the same parameter set while recognizing both well-lit and dimly lit actions. Further enhancements to the R-BERT include implementing the "delta" sampling strategy and the reconstruction technique known as Began. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves outstanding performance, outperforming existing action recognition methods even with reduced training data. Notably, the proposed method can be simplified to the basic BERT structure under certain conditions.

This report outlines the development of a Content Addressable Concurrent
Processor (CACP) based system on an Xilinx Zynq-7000 FPGA. Initially, a Content
Selectable Adder (CSA) macro was designed and integrated into the FPGA, which
was then used to create a Content Addressable Memory (CAM). By utilizing a High
Level Synthesis (HLS) approach, a Concurrent Processing Unit (CPU) was developed
and incorporated into the FPGA, effectively functioning as a parallel processor.
The CACP system was enhanced with a Network Interface Controller (NIC), which
was also implemented using the HLS, allowing the system to be part of a Network
on Chip (NoC). The developed CACP macro can be leveraged as a compact and
efficient building block for advanced FPGA systems requiring content-based
computation.

We've performed an in-depth analysis of three galaxy cores at $\rm z=2.91$ within a massive galaxy group, yielding high-resolution infrared and submillimeter data. This revealed that the galaxies exhibit extremely compact, actively star-forming cores at the centers of massive, irregularly shaped disk systems, both of which exhibit quiescent and lopsided characteristics. Consequently, these galaxies are witnessing `outside-in' quenching. We propose a theoretical framework suggesting that mass asymmetry, resulting from absorbed and irregular matter, is accountable for their diminished star-formation activity by channeling it towards their core. At the centers of these galaxies, supermassive black holes are likely responsible for their active star-formation activity, observed through their quasar-like behavior fuelled by accretion. As a result of this, galaxy mergers are predicted to accelerate and accelerate the consolidation of these galaxies' matter, transforming their star-formation activity and producing galaxy nuclei that are active and compact.

We examine the universal texture zero model of flavor, focusing on predictions made for mass and mixing patterns across generations. A key feature of this model is its ability to predict a specific value for the CP-violating phase, specifically $\delta_\mathrm{CKM}\approx 3\delta_0$. We assess the reliability of these predictions by conducting a comprehensive analysis using Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods. Our study takes into account all known mass and mixing data, along with their respective uncertainties, and even considers the previously unaccounted uncertainty associated with the CP-violating phase. By applying robust statistical methods, we are able to assess the performance of maximum likelihood estimation and assess the influence of this additional source of uncertainty. As a result, our analysis yields an estimate for $\delta_0\approx 10.5^{\circ}\,{}^{+3.5-2.5}{}^{+2.7-1.3}{}^{+3.2-1.6}{}^{+3.2-2.0}{}^{+6.8-4.0}{}^{+6.8-5.6}{}^{+12.6-8.0}{}^{+12.6-10.4}{}^{+25.2-16.0}{}^{+25.2-21.2}{}^{+50.4-32.0}{}

This study investigates the periodicity, absolute value uniqueness, and smoothness of solutions to the nonlinear elliptic equation $|\Delta f| = \lambda k(x)(|f|_{\mathbb{C}^n}^p - \mu |f|_{\mathbb{C}^n}^q)\overline{f}$ within the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$. Conditions for multiple solutions to exist are established for this nonlinear elliptic equation.

Current techniques for writing tests use static analysis to determine the conditions that need to be met. This is similar to how a Neural Network is trained with labels determined by a rule-based classification. A method is presented that connects the conditions found by static analysis with a class of problems that can be used to generate programs meeting those conditions, which is similar to how a Neural Network makes decisions based on a rule-based classification. This connection is applied to two examples: (1) writing tests for a Neural Network, and (2) writing sorters for images.

A solar event on 7th of May 2004 was found to be unusual due to its X-ray and radio emissions unlike typical observations. It also included an interesting discovery - the absence of significant hard X-rays and neutrons, despite an extremely high number of electrons being observed. Scientists used simulations to explore a hypothesis suggesting that the high electron density in the solar atmosphere could lead to their rapid annihilation through scattering processes, thus explaining the lack of neutrons and X-rays. This hypothesis proposes that electrons and positrons produced from photodisintegration are quickly balanced by Coulomb scattering, preventing the buildup of neutrons and X-rays in observation.

In both non-relativistic and relativistic hydrodynamics, the behavior of fluid modes is described by distinct equations for large and small frequencies, respectively. Under the influence of relativity, the mode behavior converges, and in the intermediate frequency range, the previously established dispersion relations exhibit convergence as well. Here, we investigate the relationship between the discrete and continuous spectra of relativistic fluid with viscosity, and we find that the quasi-transverse mode closely matches the non-relativistic transverse shear mode, and the quasi-longitudinal mode relates to the fluid's sound wave, with converging dispersion relations exhibited at higher frequencies.

Real-world data streams continue to evolve, presenting challenges in anomaly detection, especially when predefined knowledge about the data is scarce. To address this, we introduce InQMAD, a quantum-inspired anomaly detection method for data streams. In contrast to traditional anomaly detection methods that require prior definition of the data, our method leverages uncertainty to identify anomalies by computing a loss function and comparing it to a threshold. As the virtual observation of the data stream becomes more uncertain, anomalies are identified. To handle concept drift, our method updates its uncertainty using the next chest-carwining window of the data and adjusts the threshold to keep anomaly detection consistent. We evaluate our method on multiple concepts using Mikogel data streams and cross-validation, showing that our method outperforms existing anomaly detection methods in terms of F-score and outperforms a baseline concept drift detection method in terms of detection performance and concept drift measurement.

A pivotal role is played by encryption systems, which keep sensitive information secure, yet this role also makes them prime targets for government intervention, especially when the government seeks to access hidden information. Although research exists on the impact of enforcement mechanisms on security, little is known about users' technical knowledge, their cooperation with the system, and their ability to validate the authenticity of obtained data. This study seeks to examine how willing users are to grant the government access to encrypted information in response to legal threats, and in return, test users' technical knowledge, their ability to validate data, and their cooperation with the system in a simulated scenario where the government is capable of bypassing encryption. Findings reveal that while some users may be willing to grant the government access to information in response to legal threats, most users are reluctant to do so. Additionally, many users struggle to validate data even in cases where the government cannot bypass encryption. This research provides valuable insights for the design of future security systems, which should be capable of deterring the government from interfering with encrypted information.

We have developed a comprehensive framework for analyzing the measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution, based on Wigner functions. This framework provides ANS-based secret key rates and can accurately predict experimental outcomes. Its versatility allows us to incorporate real-world losses, imperfect detectors, and various quantum state preparation errors. Notably, our framework is not limited to QBER metrics and can also anticipate final secret key rates under realistic conditions, even when traditional ANS-based approaches fail to do so. We believe this framework is an invaluable reference for evaluating and comparing future measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution systems.

Building upon the work of Bakshi, Cohen, and Ron-El (STOC 2023), we've refined their PTAS approach for solving optimal valuation problems with a large number of possible values, valuations that depend on numerous variables, and sparse information. We've maintained the same constraints on the size and complexity of the given valuations, but significantly improved the runtime efficiency. We've also expanded the applicability of our technique to solve an additional optimization problem, specifically Maximum Independent Set in graphs with limited degree. Our key innovation is the development of a novel technique for strategically combining and representing valuations, which we've found to be highly flexible.

This study presents a novel, high-order numerical technique for solving the one-dimensional Fokker-Planck equation under a varying scale parameter. The method combines the Lagrange-Galerkin technique with a specific time-transformation to efficiently approximate solutions. Several implementations are displayed using different high-order Lagrange methods, both within the unit square domain and extended space. The method's stability is theoretically proven, with additional verification provided through numerical results. Furthermore, this approach is used to effectively solve a complex mean field games model describing traffic flow on a highway, including the traffic redistribution phenomenon. Successful solutions are obtained for this challenging application using both a unit square and extended domain formulation.

The surge in false news consumption has taken on particularly dangerous forms, such as unverified medical advice and inaccurately disseminated public information. Although deep learning-based techniques have achieved high accuracy in identifying false information, they often rely on available labels, overlook the vast amount of user feedback that is typically attached to news articles, and struggle with generalization to newly emitted content due to limited training data. To address these issues, we introduce an innovative false news detection method that is both emergent and multimodal, in fact the first of its kind. By leveraging user comments from multiple sources, this approach automatically learns to use new data modality - user feedback-as a means to boost performance without supervisory labeling. We propose a novel meta neural process framework to achieve this, which efficiently extracts essential information from each data modality, builds upon previous performance, and adapts to individual content needs through a carefully designed reverse dilated attention mechanism. Public information sharing on major news platforms serves as an additional data modality that can be utilized to demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, in fact it leads to significant improvements over baseline algorithms.

This research examines a one-dimensional mathematical model that describes how substances are moved by a fluid. The model is  non-isentropic  due to  considering different temperatures. We are  studying the development of shocks within this model, specifically how they form through the collision of waves with opposite movements, such as rarefaction waves and waves from the Kelvin-transform of the original equation. The study also involves demonstrating the presence and stability of a new type of transport solution that can serve as a building block for more intricate song sheets.

This research investigates the age of information in a system that updates information on a periodic basis and examines its performance when the update process takes a fixed amount of time. The study focuses on a status refreshing system where the time between updates follows a general pattern and the update time is consistent, taking into account all possible scenarios including those where the system may overwrite incomplete updates. The research utilizes both analytical methods and computer simulations to analyze the system and verifies the results through the age density function, tail recurrence relation, and average age formula. The results show that the proposed system's average age can be effectively calculated and that it can be applied to the case where updates are completed immediately. The research also compares the proposed system to the widely used geometrically distributed interarrival and service times.

This work delves into various quantum algebras that arise from a special type of set-theoretic solution to the Yang-Baxter equation, identified by Gelfand and Retakh as an algebraic quantum space associated with a smooth manifold. Building upon this framework, we establish new quasi-bialgebras using the 'quantization' and 'deformation' techniques from quantum algebra. Specifically, our 'set-theoretic quantization' yields a quantum TQFT algebra, while our 'set-theoretic deformation' results in quantum dilogarithm algebras and twisted Drinfel'd doubles of lower triangular matrix algebras, all defined over suitable smooth manifolds or deformed semisimple algebraic varieties.

The technique of complementary sensing, first introduced by Bartosiewicz in 1998, has been demonstrated to efficiently utilize interference while maintaining an effective signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio. Throughout its development, researchers have primarily utilized complementary sequences, despite array processing generally achieving higher computational efficiency and signal-to-noise ratio than sequence processing. In 2017, an approach was proposed to utilize complementary arrays with linear interferers, however it required specifically designed array configurations and was limited to near-field scenarios. This research develops novel complementary array designs based on Golay patterns, providing a more flexible and versatile complementary processing approach. Two complementary designs are presented: an elemental design utilizing Golay pairs of phase sequences, and a composite design combining multiple identical elemental designs. A new complementary criterion is proposed to broaden the scope of eligible phase sequences, allowing the composite design greater flexibility. When compared to traditional complementary sequence designs, the proposed complementary arrays offer broader design options, simpler design processes, and more flexible configurations. Simulation results effectively demonstrate the proposed approach's capability to null out interferers and enhance the signal detection performance.

Quantum interference in single-electron transistors based on silicon atom point contacts exhibits a unique feature, known as valley interference, which can be seen in the side peaks of conductance. Through precise measurements, the relative height of these peaks provides information about the relative phase between the two valleys in silicon. It is discovered that this relative phase is influenced by electron spin, which is determined by applying a magnetic field and varying it manually. Under conditions where the two valleys are symmetric, a non-Lorentzian lineshape is observed in the valley-dependent phase. Notably, this line shape deviates from the expected form when the relative height of the peaks is off-balanced. By utilizing a spin-polarized current, it is possible to swap the relative phase between the two valleys, achieving a cross-control between the valleys and the electron spin which is crucial for controlling the spin-dependent conductance in the main valley valley, and can be controlled over a broad range, and may have implications for designing efficient quantum devices based on silicon.

Complex systems consisting of multiple interacting components are prevalent in various fields including economics, biology, and social sciences. Understanding how these complex systems operate is further complicated by their intermittent and unstable nature. This paper explores the potential of advanced machine learning techniques for modeling and understanding complex systems that are in a state of constant change. Specifically, we review a range of Machine Learning methods suitable for analyzing these systems, with a focus on Graph Neural Network-based algorithms that can model interactions between system components and learn from dynamic systems. We discuss the strengths and limitations of these approaches and highlight the need for integration of complementary ML methods to tackle the challenges associated with modeling complex systems.

We introduce two novel functions within the set of non-negative integer partitions that have specific properties. These functions are called weakly increasing and strictly increasing. Any given partition can be associated with an abstract directed graph where each node represents an number within the partition and the edges represent the relationships between these numbers. The properties of this graph, known as 1-Lipschitz graph, determine the increasing nature of a function. The notion of partition multiplication leads to the directed cycle graph and the mixed graph with both directed and undirected edges. The last part of the paper delves into the implications of these concepts in the context of rational homotopy theory, particularly in relation to the formal moduli space of rational homotopy types.

Computational imaging techniques, when paired with advanced simulation and neural imaging methods, can accurately portray physical injuries. However, creating realistic synthetic data for complex injuries likepediatric head injuries remains a difficult task due to the diversity of possible injury patterns. We propose an innovative, step-by-step approach to generate realistic CT images of pediatric brain injuries using a series of neural networks and an adversarial learning framework. By training a series of auto-encoders and an adversarial network in stages, we can accurately synthesize complex injuries and a wide range of injury types. Our results, when compared to a large dataset of real imaging data, show high accuracy in capturing the overall injury patterns, with an F-score of 0.732.

Quantum correlations found in entangled states offer a uniquely strong form of nonlocal behavior that surpasses the limits set by local hidden variables. This quality becomes increasingly obvious when using entangled states as a resource in various tasks that exploit the uniquely quantum nature of entanglement. One such resource is quasi-maximally entangled states found in bipartite systems, which show the largest violations of local realism limits and allow for perfect measurement outcomes. Nevertheless, these highly effective states are extremely sensitive to measurement inaccuracies and don't exist in practical multi-partite systems. Our novel approach shies away from purity requirements and instead focuses on unextendible product bases in systems of multiple parties. This finding demonstrates that strong quantum nonlocality can be seen in three, four, and five-party systems where some elements share bipartite systems with different types of dimensions. Because this discovery happens in such practical setups, it highlights the potential for measurements to accurately demonstrate the limits of local realism based on the entangled state's ability to produce impossible outcomes for local hidden variables and perfectly distinguish the state from separable states.

The speed at which robust multi-agent planning algorithms operate is crucial for applying them to real-time applications like the Fifth Data Release of the astrobots safe coordination experiment for the Sloan Digital Survey. We are able to evaluate their effectiveness and potential by using a fleet of physical robots named astrobots on the SDSS V floor. Our analysis gathers complete traversal times for various areas of the space, taking into consideration all possible starting and ending positions for the astrobots.

GP 2 is a version of the GP programming language, which has a syntax similar to Python but executes much faster. It achieves this faster execution through a technique called Code Generation, where GP 2 converts the program into a more efficient form before running it. GP 2 does this by converting the program into an Intermediate Representation and then using a dynamic Object-oriented interpretation system to execute it. Its code generation process has a flexible object model that allows it to handle Python-like grammar easily. This has led to GP 2 being used in the Open Source Version of Canare, a Can Bus Scanner.

To enhance information retrieval and analysis, extracting key features from content is a critical step. Deep neural networks have become a popular choice for this task due to their ability to automatically generate high-quality representations. Nevertheless, developing such a model requires a significant investment of time and resources, as it typically requires a large annotated dataset. In this work, a new model is presented that can extract both textual and non-textual features from various media types, including audio, video, and images. The model employs a contrastive learning approach to create a universal feature representation that is robust and versatile. By leveraging pre-existing high-quality content and utilizing auxiliary information, the model demonstrates an improved performance compared to traditional extraction methods and is capable of adapting to different tasks with minimal data and manual intervention.
We establish the normal quotient graph property for an extensive class of twisted wreath type groups, specifically infinite collections of twisted wreath type groups.

Group lasso and its variants have been extensively studied for solving
  categorical data selection problems.  Despite significant progress since 2010,
  most state-of-the-art methods lack a certain level of efficiency when dealing
  with large-scale datasets, especially those with many groups.  In this paper, we
  introduce an innovative enhancement to the group lasso framework, focusing on
  efficient solution methods.  By leveraging simple yet straightforward
  transformations, we can reformulate the group lasso problem to retain its
  equivalence, allowing for easier optimization.  Further enhancements to the
  basic group lasso formulation involve adding constraints to promote
  sparsity.  In this paper, we develop customized versions of the alternating
  direction method of multipliers (ADMM) to solve these formulations, along with
  a customized proximal gradient method for the basic group lasso problem.  Our
  results from numerical experiments demonstrate superior performance of our
  proposed methods over current state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy
  and efficiency, even for datasets with thousands of groups.

Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved human-like performance on numerous NLP tasks. However, there's a concern that LLMs' parameters may be contaminated by inaccurate and biased information from web sources. As professional-compiled structured knowledge contains NERs that are verified and organized, it's beneficial to firmly correct any inaccuracies present in LLMs' parameters through a process known as Structureized Knowledge Injection (SKI). This process is tailored to the unique characteristics of structured data, enabling the preservation of relationship consistency during the injection process. We explored various strategies to adapt LLMs' inherent capabilities to efficiently absorb large quantities of knowledge. Our comprehensive evaluation demonstrates that SKI significantly surpasses conventional fine-tuning methods on downstream tasks, with empirical evidence showing a substantial enhancement by around 2.33 times in averaged F1 score over BERT-based LLMs across three different structured knowledge adaptation processes and seven downstream benchmarks.

This article introduces a novel model for describing anomalous diffusion processes.
The model utilizes a specific type of nonlocal operator to define interaction intensities between elements, where the distances are scaled inversely to the fourth power.
As the scaling factor approaches zero, the model converges to a different framework that involves long-range interactions described by a fractional operator.
A key distinction between these two frameworks lies in their treatment of boundary effects, which the novel model accurately accounts for, whereas the fractional operator fails to do so effectively.

This research addresses the challenge of seamlessly connecting panoramic images under the influence of gravity. Although various methods exist for solving this problem, they often lack a unified approach. We tackle this problem using an optimized framework to determine key parameters. By directly estimating the panoramic geometry and the location of images in a 3D space, we can efficiently connect them. Using a minimal solution, we reduce the number of required correspondences between images to four. We also explore the problem's geometric implications and the influence of noise on results. A linear solution and non-linear optimization are developed to enhance accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, including its performance under artificially induced noise and its application in connecting images captured by移动 devices without the use of gyroscopes.

This study develops two combinatorial tools used in the process of removing singularities from a specific type of mathematical function called an Eisenstein series, for a specific group, $GL(n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$. The focus is on the near diagonal contribution within the spherical decomposition of this contribution. The underlying purposes of these tools are to determine the non-zero boundary values for a specific type of number, an $L$-function, on a specific line, and to establish the equidistribution of a specific type of mathematical object, a parabolic subgroup, within another subgroup, in the case where the boundary value is zero, for a specific type of mathematical object, a cuspidal automorphic representation, for which the associated parameter is not equivalent to a character, in the case where the boundary value is zero, for a specific type of mathematical object, an irreducible automorphic representation, for which the associated parameter is not equivalent to a character, in the case where the boundary value is zero.

This study examines the decline in inhibitory subthalamic nucleus (STN) to globus pallidus externus (GPe) feedback in Parkinson's patients, which disrupts the balance between excitatory and inhibitory signals in the STN-GPe network. As a result, pathological $\beta$-oscillations emerge in this network. Our research aims to recreate these features using a biophysical computational model of the STN-GPe network, which is relevant to patients and based on data from healthy common marmoset monkeys. Initially, we validated the model by simulating the natural $\beta$-oscillations observed in post-optic tract lesioned marmosets. We then modified the model to replicate the altered parameters found in Parkinson's patients, including the decrease in inhibitory STN to GPe feedback. When we reduced this feedback below a critical threshold in the model, we successfully recreated the $\beta$-oscillations seen in patients. Furthermore, when we increased it, the pathological $\delta$-oscillations were reinstated. Our study establishes key requirements for treating these disorders by stimulating the STN to GPe feedback connections, providing a framework for future research and potential treatments.

When converting vector line data to raster images, anti-aliasing techniques help improve the visual quality. However, existing methods fall short when it comes to rendering joined lines. This study examines anti-aliasing line rendering at joined points and presents a tailored algorithm for achieving this. By comparing it against the conventional method, our approach is found to generate significantly smaller color variations, resulting in noticeably reduced visual quality differences. Further, by incorporating this algorithm into map visualization workflows, we observe distinct differences in visual quality, with the refined method better capturing the shape of shapes, and potentially conveying different semantic information. To further facilitate adoption, we've released our algorithm as an open-source extension for Mapbox GL JS.

Our team utilized the KOOLS-IFU on Seimei Telescope for integral field unit (IFU) imaging of nine ultra/distant lobe galaxies at low redshifts (less than 0.04). These galaxies, characterized by high infrared emissions, were selected based on their location within the Compton Sample. From our observations, we obtained spatially resolved spectral data, from which we derived redshifts, removed the effect of Earth's atmosphere, and calculated a low-resolution continuum across the visible spectrum. By comparing our findings with existing HST spectroscopic data, we discovered a correlation between the ratio of gallium to aluminum and the logarithm of far-infrared to aluminum fluxes. Additionally, we discovered a relationship between the aluminum flux and the infrared brightness, as well a relationship between aluminum and far-infrared fluxes.

The multivariate interpolation operator is traditionally constructed using piecewise linear functions to approximate absolute differences between values. In this study, we develop a novel, transcendental interpolation function rooted in the exponential function. This innovative approach enables the creation of a global interpolation operator that maintains the original function's shape, utilizing the exponential hyperbolic tangent function. Furthermore, we establish convergence rates for both the newly proposed interpolation operator and its alternative, linear counterpart. In addition, we demonstrate the efficiency and accuracy of the newly proposed method through the approximation of a non-periodic function in two dimensions.

Recent advancements in Convolutional Neural Networks have effectively utilized Image-based techniques for predicting various outcomes including vehicle accidents, traffic conditions, and weather.
To train a Weather classification model, we need labeled datasets that pair images with corresponding weather information. However, public data sources often lack explicit metadata on images, making it challenging to associate nearby weather observations with a particular image. Consequently, compiling a robust dataset for Weather classification is a significant hurdle in applying Image-based methods to this field.
To address this issue, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of multiple weather datasets including the open-source datasets from the PyArt and PyCO3 packages, as well as the commercially available Google Photos dataset. We then developed an innovative approach utilizing the YOLO object detector to link weather observations to a particular image, along with data augmentation techniques to expand each dataset to 100,000 labeled images for each weather category under study including Fog, Rain, Snow, and Clear skies.
Our model achieved higher accuracy compared to the best results reported in recent papers on the standard Image classification datasets from Imagenet and ILSVRC. When evaluated on the diverse range of Google Photos images, our algorithm displayed superior accuracy in contrast to algorithms utilizing Near-Infrared (NIR) data and Color Meteorological Aerogauge (C-MAG) data. Additionally, our model exhibited cost-effective performance requiring significantly fewer computational resources than the best results obtained using NIR and C-MAG data.

To improve the quality of low-fidelity recordings, a Multi-Path Convolution Recurrent Network was previously proposed, but it had limitations due to its single-path convolutional structure, which hindered its ability to effectively process the sequence-dependent characteristics of non-stationary sounds. In response, a Dual-Path Convolution Recurrent Network was developed that addresses these shortcomings by integrating two parallel network branches: one that utilizes LSTM to handle temporal features and another that extracts spectral characteristics through spectral convolutional layers. Furthermore, the incorporation of dilated convolutions enables more extensive temporal and frequency range coverage within the network. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in objective and subjective metrics, including approximately 0.3 enhancements in PESQ and MOS scores and nearly 3 dB increase in SNR. The new architecture was also optimized for efficiency through knowledge distillation techniques, resulting in reduced latency and memory usage while maintaining high performance.

A new statistics methodology is introduced, focused on the size of dark matter halos, to investigate how their scales are affected by non-gravitational forces, and consider the mass of neutrinos in relation to various $f(R)$ gravity models. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we evaluate the reliability of this method and its ability to accurately assess the impact of these forces on halo density profiles. With specific choices of $f(R)$ gravity models and neutrino masses, we end up with theoretical predictions that align well with actual data when adjusted for biases. Furthermore, we can distinguish between the two types of modified gravity and neutrino mass effects based on the performance of these predictions. Lastly, we can determine the effective mass range of neutrinos for different $f(R)$ gravity models through this evaluation, and our results show a clear difference in the accuracy of identification at various turn-around radii.

Recently proposed multi-fluid models have been suggested for improving current single-column and 3D atmospheric convection simulation methods. A crucial factor in boundary layer dynamics is the presence of rising warm air and rising as well as falling cold air currents. A two-fluid model could address this by separating the temperature-based fluid behavior into two distinct components: cool and warm. This study examines a 2D Rayleigh-Benard convection simulation using a two-fluid model, where each fluid component is treated with different physical properties, including mass advection. Various model configurations are tested by adjusting the resolution and rate of cooling the cool and warm fluids. A transition point is identified at a critical resolution and results are compared to single-fluid simulations with and without convection. Furthermore, present models are limited by the need to match the mass of the cool and warm air during convection, which is not representative of real atmospheric conditions. Nonetheless, present models show promising potential for improving atmospheric convection simulation, subject to further optimization and testing.

The quantum states of separate systems can become intricately connected through their individual evolutions, a phenomenon known as sincere entanglement. To investigate this, we utilized two independently operating pairs of non-interacting atoms within distinct cavities that do not interact with each other, leveraging the varying J-C interactions. By carefully manipulating the systems, we observed that this entanglement could accurately reflect the degree of I-NC interaction between the two atomic pairs. Notably, two distinct methods were identified to predict the optimal conditions for evaluating this interplay. Furthermore, when QI was used as a control, our proposed scheme exhibited robustness against various types of noise, making it ideal for processing information in a reliable manner.

The Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) detector in the LHC Experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider underwent an upgrade, transforming it from a legacy system to a fully calibrated synchronous setup, during the period of Phase 1 in 2016-2018. This transformation included the replacement of the pixel detector, with the new system featuring 148800 individual detector modules, organized into triangles and triangles modified by an added blade structure, installed between June 2015 and January 2017. Between these dates, proton collisions at the LHC's interaction points yielded data at center-of-energy values of 7 and 13 TeV. The analysis presented here examines the reconstruction of these modified modules using data collected at 13 TeV in 2016, with a collected luminosity of 36 fb-1. The reconstruction process involved resetting the readout systems and reconfiguring them to match the new detector layout, with software and hardware readout firmware developed independently for this purpose. The analysis further investigates the resolution of hit points and global alignment after accounting for interaction points, with results indicating that certain components met alignment thresholds with residual distances of less than 10 µm.

A key test for the Kall\'en-Lehman spectral representation of the SU(2) gluonium has been developed, specifically for a scalar state with no color charge. A theoretical formula follows, linking the real part of the transverse correlator of the SU(2) gluon field strength to the sum of the squared decay constants, $\mathcal{F}_n$, of all the linear, point-like, neutral states, arranged in towers, with increasing mass. A crucial condition for this representation is that the gluon propagation distance must be much smaller than the inverse energy scales of these state masses. A direct, observable consequence of this formulation is that the highest excited state's energy, denoted as $M_0$, should be significantly lower than the perturbative peak position, $\sqrt{12}\,M_{\pi}$, which could provide a clearer definition of hadron thresholds. A precise calculation of the relevant dispersion relation for the gluonium has been performed for the SU(2) case, using the established data for the lowest-lying neutral meson towers. This enables a precise estimation of $M_0$, with an expected value of approximately $6.33\,M_{\pi}$, and it should be possible to experimentally verify this by measuring the relevant spectral function.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions towards them and their rivals.
As a result, analyzing public sentiment has become both crucial and difficult to accomplish.
In this paper, we present a novel approach for classifying the sentiment expressed in Twitter
tweets as positive, negative, or neutral. Our method involves extracting features from tweets
using N-grams, and these features are then used as input for a K-nearest neighbor, support vector
machine, or long short-term memory network to determine the sentiment expressed. We were
able to achieve the most favorable accuracy with our proposed method that utilizes the extraction
of word-level features and feeds them to an LSTM network connected to a softmax layer.

A non-linear charged black hole in four-dimensional Anti-de Sitter space is analyzed using a power-law form for its electrostatic interaction. A shade thermodynamic geometry is proposed to evaluate the geometric properties of the black hole's thermodynamic behavior through the Curvature scalar and Bistate entropy through its respective factors. It is found that as the charge increases, both geometric measures show a shift in their balance between expanding and contracting, indicating a phase transition linked to Weyl symmetry and information changes. Furthermore, both measures are seen to be influenced by both the charge and the parameter defining the non-linear field, indicating complex interactions within the black hole's thermodynamic system.

Tomography is an essential non-invasive imaging technique used to visualize the internal structure of objects, with applications in both medical and industrial fields. Recent advances in low-dose X-ray computed tomography enable the study of live processes and dynamic events. In this work, we apply quantum tomography to coherent states and classical tomography to radiographic images of real-time processes, demonstrating how to extract additional information from low-dose X-ray CT scans to reveal phenomena not visible in standard CT images. We show that reducing entanglement between scanned systems can be observed and quantify through changes in their tomograms, and propose using CT scans to simultaneously capture both observable and non-observable aspects of a process by leveraging the extra information contained in them.

Building a search system that provides answers to queries via dialogue requires a new approach that incorporates the specific roles and goals of both the conversation participant and the system, as well as the overarching objective of the conversation. This is achieved by leveraging a large-scale language model to have the conversation follow natural flow, while also leveraging model predictions to ensure the system is moving towards the overall goal of the conversation. This is demonstrated by leveraging a conversational assistant model and a conversation goal specification system to build one that meets the specific requirements of the conversation. A new method is proposed that incorporates both the role and the overall goal of the conversation into the evaluation of the system's performance, resulting in a highly efficient system that provides answers to queries via dialogue that meets the specific requirements of the conversation, as evidenced by experimental results on a conversational question-answering task.

Choosing effective strategies to pest control is a complex decision made by farmers that necessitates evaluating the risks and benefits of various methods. Nonetheless, traditional approaches to agricultural decision-making often solely focus on economic gains, neglecting other crucial factors like environmental and social impacts. Moreover, the high uncertainty of yield and quality predictions based on pest management plans is usually inadequately addressed. In this research, we introduce an innovative method to assess pest management strategies that incorporates multiple criteria and accounts for uncertainty through probability distributions of potential yield and quality outcomes. We then apply this method to strawberry disease management in a commercial setting, where we assess the strategies in consideration of farmers' preferences, the methods of assessment used, and different pest pressure scenarios. According to the results, the optimal strategy as per the method proposed is to always apply the best treatment due to its high potential to maximize yields with minimal risk.

As the popularity of internet tourism videos continues to grow, developing realistic and engaging virtual tourism videos via video conferencing technologies has become increasingly challenging.  One of the key challenges is rotating users within a 360-degree video environment to optimal viewing angles that align with cultural and social norms.  Existing approaches rely on analyzing local visual cues within the video, which are often insufficient for accurate perspective prediction.  We have discovered that subtitles present within the video provide valuable information about the scene's overall content and can significantly enhance perspective prediction accuracy.  We present an innovative two-stage method that initially extracts meaningful information from subtitles and then integrates them with visual cues using learned features to predict accurate perspective angles within the video. Our method has demonstrated superior performance when pitted against alternative methods that solely utilize visual cues or employ less effective enhancement techniques.

Tensor network methods have commonly been used to represent complex quantum systems, particularly in calculating the thermal behavior and temporal evolution of these systems. Despite their success, these methods often struggled with accuracy at the boundary regions. A new type of tensor network approach has been developed, which utilizes a localized tensor type that can precisely handle boundary regions while maintaining efficiency. This novel method is applicable to one-dimensional quantum systems exhibiting U(1) unitary unitary group invariance, U(N) symmetry or when the system's unitary group can be approximated by a smaller, manageable subset. This new approach has resulted in accurate representations of thermal states and the outcomes of time evolution in quantum systems, as evidenced by long-lasting vibrational movements and thermalization behavior related to logarithmic corrections, as well as thermal distributions based on Kempelen functions.

We develop a decoupling theory for a class of operations known as restricted efficacy operations, which includes effects that an agent cannot control due to information deficits or limitations in agency. To address this type of problem, we can apply decisions under uncertainty, though this requires characterizing the scope of possible world states. We observe that more limited efficacy generally narrows the set of potential world states, as increased control equals increased information about the state of the world. Consequently, restricted efficacy decoupling involves agent action that minimizes the information required to achieve the goal, given the available world-state information. Our decoupling theory decouples the agent's objective from their limited efficacy by identifying the set of potential world states that include the goal given their current knowledge, then deciding on an action that isolates the goal given this set of possible world states. We validate our theory with examples that illustrate the connection between our work and work in decision-making, including Markov decision processes.

We investigate various aspects of anisotropic capillary surfaces, focusing on their relationship with shape operators and variations in surface area under specific constraints. An inequality resembling a Minkowski inequality is derived for anisotropic spheres, with a corresponding geometric interpretation for a sharp related inequality for willian surfaces. A new form of anisotropic dilational variance will be defined, and connections with the anisotropic Minkowski inequality and a recent equality case will be established. A new inequality resembling a Minkowski inequality is proven for surfaces, with the relationship to existing inequalities being examined.

The Microscope space test for the weak equivalence principle involves measuring the difference in acceleration of two test masses as they orbit the Earth. 
To understand how different factors, such as acceleration noise and acceleration glitches, impact the test's sensitivity, we developed a simplified model of the experiment and conducted a virtual test using accelerated signals similar to those actually observed. 
Our analysis reveals that acceleration glitches with specific characteristics can be detected with high confidence through our simplified model. 
However, other types of glitches may remain unnoticed by our basic analysis but can be identified through more comprehensive methods. 
It was also found that in order to achieve a $10^{-15}$ accuracy in testing the weak equivalence principle, it will be necessary to mitigate the effects of different types of acceleration noise and glitches. This could be accomplished by utilizing specific types of accelerometers rather than trying to compensate for the observed effects through data analysis techniques.

We examine the steady-state behavior of autonomous microscopic structures composed of multiple particle units that interact with each other, located near a boundary separated into two areas with differing levels of activity. This setup creates a chemical-like gradient that influences structures based on their shape and internal connections. Some pairs of particles within these assemblies can move freely across the boundary, while others are restricted to one side, affecting their ability to stay together and respond to activity gradients. Positive differences in activity trap certain structures against the boundary, while moderately active structures can be found throughout both sides. Increasing activity can result in a shift from accumulated structures at the boundary to those dispersed on the activity-high side. Significant internal reorganization can also take place within some structures in response to the activity level, allowing them to preserve their overall number of units but change their arrangement. These findings offer valuable insights for applying active matter as a model system for cells that respond to their surroundings and can be trapped or transformed upon encountering a chemical boundary.

We define the strong shortest path collection concept for graphs and explore its properties in certain types of graphs and networks. A key metric, the strong shortest path collection coefficient, is introduced to rate the efficiency of such collections. Additionally, we analyze specific scenarios where some graphs do not have a shortest path collection but can have an extended collection by adding one more edge. We also investigate n-mesh networks and a variant, missing a corner n-mesh networks, determining their collection capabilities and efficiency ratings.

A nonperturbative effect has been identified that affects the high-logarithm behavior of color dipole TMD PDF in the small-x region.  An investigation into the impact of infrared renormalons on the small-x dynamics of the color dipole TMD PDF leads to an issue where the large logarithmic terms in the PDF's evolution, specifically the DGLAP and BFKL evolutions, contend with the non-logarithmic terms generated by spatial Fourier transformation, resulting in an inconsistency at high logarithms. To resolve this conflict, a modification proposed involves adding a damping factor, $x_{\perp}^{2\alpha_{\rm eff}}$, to the non-logarithmic term, allowing for an increase in the logarithmic accuracy to next-to-next-to-leading logarithm (NNLL) level for $x \to 0$. Without the proposed modification, only the leading logarithm accuracy can be maintained, whereas implementing it restores the three-power counting validity even without the $2\alpha_{\rm eff}$ term to $x^2 \sim 1/Q^2$ scale. Furthermore, the derived formulae for both the small-$x$ and intermediate-$x$ regimes can be directly compared to the derivative of the dipole TMD correlation matrix, establishing a connection to the impact parameter space evolution of TMD PDF and allowing for an investigation into the interplay of DGLAP and BFKL evolutions in the impact parameter space.
We analyze the frog model on rooted d-ary trees, noting that its critical density is precisely 1 for trees with d >= 3, but on binary trees (d=2), the critical density is approximately 1.203.

Researchers are focusing on nonreciprocal light propagation in ultrafast optical systems to rapidly control the flow of light within the circuit. Although conventional methods using magnetic fields achieve nonreciprocity, they are limited due to the need for external fields and their impact on light over wide frequency ranges. A new class of material that displays intrinsic nonreciprocity over broad spectra without the need for magnetic fields is very rare. Our discovery of nonreciprocal halo generation in giant halo lattices made from these materials provides an intrinsic nonreciprocal interface between light propagating in different directions. Our models and experimental results demonstrate significant photo-magnetic halos with distinct spatial shapes generated by red and blue light separately. Since giant halo lattices are sensitive to symmetry breaking, the proposed system may offer a highly efficient and tunable interface for coupling to neighboring circuits over a wide range of frequencies.

A decision-based model of knowledgable humans is presented, and it's demonstrated that existing general knowledge can be effectively transferred to a new task with minimal adaptation, utilizing very little additional knowledge.

Researchers have studied the decay of $B^0_s$ particles into the combination of $\bar{D}^0$ and $K^0_S$ particles, specifically $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decays. Initially presented as evidence for this process at the SLD, further confirmation comes from analyzing events where the $\bar{D}^0$ particle decays into $K^+\pi^-$ and the $\bar{D}^{*0}$ particle decays into $\bar{D}^0\pi^0$ with the $\bar{D}^0$ decaying into $K^+\pi^-$. By reconstructing the $\bar{D}^0$ or $D^0$ particles in these events, researchers found strong evidence for the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decay through analyzing the invariant mass distribution of the $\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ and $D^0\bar{K}^0_S$ pairs. This research provides constraints on certain parameters, including the average $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decay rate and the minimum significance of the $D^0\bar{K}^0_S$ peak. These results were displayed through relevant plots and tables.

We introduce an efficient algorithm that constructs a lattice of submodules for a given multiplicity-free module over a group ring, based on provided matrices. A key aspect of our method is a direct formula for calculating submodules, based on an innovative expression of the group elements. This approach ensures that the lattice constructed by our algorithm conforms to a distributive pattern.

A geodetic set of a graph G is defined by its unique property where the shortest path between any two vertices within the set connects all vertices of G. Identifying whether a given subgraph of a graph forms a geodetic set is a well-studied parameterized problem, especially when near-optimal solutions are unattainable due to NP-completeness. In contrast, the recognition problem of determining if a graph has a geodetic subset has various applications but remains sparsely investigated. This paper explores computing the geodetic recognition number of a graph, classifying several graph families based on this computation, and presenting a geodetic recognition number algorithm for cubic planar graphs within a polynomial time frame. Our key findings include proving the geodetic recognition number computability for circular and generalized circular arc graphs, while also demonstrating its difficulty for block graphs and tree-block graphs through analysis.

A key goal of imitation learning is to replicate the expertise of human experts by observing their actions. However, due to the vast number of task scenarios it is impossible to cover, there always exists an inherent lack of information in datasets. As such, it is crucial to acknowledge and manage this inherent uncertainty when developing imitation learning methods. In order to address this issue, we present TRAIL, an algorithm capable of identifying the most efficient action among multiple equally probable options at any given state. TRAIL finds the optimal action through the analysis of a dataset that is generated by merging two distinct types of data: demonstrations and independent task experiences. By leveraging efficient similarity-based similarity measures, TRAIL can pinpoint the actions that are closest to the demonstrated actions in situations that are analogous to the current state. Furthermore, theoretical analysis of the algorithm reveals its ability to converge to an optimal solution as the dataset grows larger. In addition, we show that the algorithm is capable of achieving significant improvements over existing methods in evaluations conducted on both artificial and real-world datasets.

Reinforcement learning efficiency can be significantly enhanced through imitation training, which consists of updating policy networks based on expert demonstrations. However, collecting and labeling extensive demonstrations from actual experts can be time-consuming and labor-intensive. To address this limitation, we present a method known as Co-Imitation Training, in which an agent's policy is refined using demonstrations created by another artificial expert. Our experimentally evaluated results show that Co-Imitation Training yields significant performance improvements compared to standard imitation learning and outperforms certain self-supervised learning methods.

This research addresses how to accurately calculate the performance metrics of pressure-controlled acoustic coupling systems, also known as PAC codes. These codes are used to improve signal transmission in difficult environmental conditions. The accurate evaluation of PAC codes is challenging due to the pressure-controlled mechanism altering standard performance metrics like correlation width and side lobe patterns. By modeling the pressure-controlled process using Chebyshev polynomials, the authors developed an efficient method for determining the performance metrics of PAC codes. The proposed algorithm significantly reduces the computational time while providing precise results, showing less than 1% deviation from directly computed results for certain cases. The researchers showcased their approach with numerical results, showcasing the raised cosine PAC code's benefits in reducing main lobe width by about 30% compared to standard PAC codes.

Previous work on incorporating reinforcement learning (RL) into translation models has been limited by the high cost of calculating the RL signal's impact on subsequent decisions due to the large action space in neural machine translation. This issue can be mitigated by utilizing frame stacking, similar approaches, and large action spaces in RL. We propose integrating these concepts and suggest two methods to reduce the action space in translation models. Firstly, the use of beam search can be replaced with the selection of multiple future translations rather than individual words. Secondly, the concept of state can be redefined to be translation-specific rather than source sentence-specific. The proposed ideas are validated through experiments and results show that both concepts can be effective. Furthermore, the first method yields performance comparable to the conventional RL-based translation models. The proposed framework can be viewed as an innovative way of applying RL to translation models and opens up room for the application of other advanced RL techniques.

A cost-effective and capable setup for industrial robots involves a depth camera, yet often comes uncalibrated. The lack of calibration makes it difficult to accurately predict the object's position in 3D space by simply using the robot's world frame. Although there are methods to calibrate systems with additional markers and a known tool pose, these methods are inflexible and costly. The proposed approach, in contrast, relies on a markerless technique that requires no special markers or pre-trained models, instead it is based on self-supervised learning with a simulation and can be applied to any system. The author demonstrates that the algorithm not only calibrates the camera but also estimates the tool pose, outperforming method from the literature in accuracy and efficiency and demonstrating versatility with a variety of unstructured scenarios.

We introduce a new concept called the QFS-region for a pair of matrices, which encompasses two positive definite matrices that share the same binary similarity diagonal form. If two matrices fall within the QFS-region, they can be transformed into each other through a sequence of elementary block row and column operations. This definition enables us to establish the invariance of positive definite binary forms under the action of general linear groups over any rings, which in turn can be applied to explore the complexity of computing these forms.

The increasing polarization in society, particularly within the online environment, has significant implications for how individuals obtain news. A large-scale study involving more than 10 million U.S. users and their consumed news articles from 1,311 major outlets between 2016 and 2020, reveals valuable insights into the polarization phenomenon. By analyzing the content of the consumed articles using topic models and measuring their political slant, researchers discovered distinct consumption patterns among users. These patterns are correlated with user demographics and their consumed sources of news. Additionally, investigators identified two key dynamics at play within user behavior related to political division: users tend to be exposed to increasingly polarizing content over time within their news consumption, and users with similar ideological views often engage in banded consumption of the same news sources. This phenomenon has an unexpected outcome - it tends to diminish user diversity within the same community. As a result, users are likely to become exposed to more diverse sources of news that appeal to various demographic groups.

We have developed a scar version of the Thompson group V's word puzzle, using a modified tuple of reordering rules. This specific scalar version of the group's word puzzle is unmanageably complex, according to our finding. Additionally, various sub-problems of the management-level puzzle display disparate levels of complexity, involving issues ranging from easy to unsolvable. These issues include some speech problems within the group's subgroups that are insurmountably difficult to solve. We've also found that the group's subwords can be solved with limited success, but this level of success cannot be achieved with any manageable level of effort.

The study of open quantum systems under periodic driving forces is an enticing field that has gained significant interest. However, a full understanding of these systems in steady-state driven conditions has been hindered until now. As a first step, we set out to create and analyze a theoretical model for a driven two-level system within a real-world context that has previously been observed but not fully understood. A qubit, when subjected to periodic measurement and relaxation and then verified to be in a persistent, complex, steady-state that emerges slowly over time as a result of its interaction with its environment. Both non-invasive real-time experiments and comprehensive theoretical simulations reveal this driven, stable condition. These simulations further shed light on the intricate dynamics at play during the formation of this driven steady-state. As a result, we establish and validate a crucial distinction between systems that are in a driven steady-state and those that are merely in a transient driven state. Additionally, we investigate whether this driven steady-state condition can be utilized for practical applications, including quantum error correction, enhanced quantum control, and accelerated algorithm implementation, or if it can be harnessed for new sensing techniques that take advantage of its unique properties, such as its robustness, or if it can be employed to understand and explore other open quantum systems under periodic driving forces.

This research explores various complex submanifolds within the Euclidean space,
specifically focusing on biharmonic hypersurfaces. The study investigates several
advanced mathematical concepts including invariant, recurrent, semi-invariant,
null-correlated, conformal, and recurrent conformal 1-forms. The research analyzes
the interactions between these concepts and establishes conditions for a hypersurface
to be considered minimal. Additionally, this study demonstrates that certain types
of invariant, recurrent, and semi-invariant 1-forms cannot coexist with the
structure of a biharmonic hypersurface as described in Theorem 1. Furthermore,
this research reveals that a special type of recurrent 1-form can lead to the
existence of a global biharmonic submanifold in the Euclidean space. This study also
examines several examples of biharmonic hypersurfaces in the Euclidean space that
are associated with different types of recurrent 1-forms.

The concept of a unique idempotent matrix is well-established for positive definite matrices, but extending this to non-commuting matrices presents a challenge. We introduce the framework of a ring R to analyze idempotent elements and expand this to an 'idempotent idempotancy raising pair' within specific subroutines of R. Focusing on the idempotency idempotancy raising pair, we examine a polynomial expression p/q that can elevate an idempotent element to a power n within subroutines containing the quotient of polynomials with coefficients in C. By applying this framework to the idempotency idempotancy raising pair of C<X>, we demonstrate that certain idempotent polynomials can be represented by rational expressions. Extending this analysis to matrix rings C<X>M, we show that specific idempotent matrices can be idempotency idempotently raised to a positive integer power n.

In this study, we expand the Standard Model by adding two new components: a finite-scale invariant gluon anomaly for a complex scalar called the axion, and an $\mathcal{A}\overline{\nu}_R\gamma_R$ interaction for right-handed sterile neutrinos. This approach allows us to analyze the effects of these new particles on the early universe's phase transitions and cosmic microwave background, as well as direct and indirect observations of particles. By examining these factors and a third parameter - the right-handed neutrino mass, we map the parameter space for the axion and sterile neutrino. Notably, we find a new form of matter consisting of axion-filled gravitational condensate stars, which could be identified as potential candidates for dark matter. Also, we predict a rare phenomenon where the right-handed neutrino decays produce high-energy photons, which may be observable through future observations of the Milky Way's nucleus and other deep sky surveys.

Between March 2019 and September 2019, the LAMOST performed a high-precision density measurement survey using four K2 plates, specifically focusing on scientific domains like the LAMOST Q-Gratings and prior to the insertion of the flux collector. During this 183-day period, the team carried out power supply checks and system alignments, resulting in a clean, bias-corrected time series of 20 days or less. By eliminating known frequencies and their harmonics from the data, the LAMOST achieved a typical bias density of around $3 \times 10^{-4}$, marking a significant improvement over the previous $1 \times 10^{-3}$ standard set by the LAMOST Q-Gratings. With the removal of gaps larger than 1 hour from the data, the bias decreased to $1 \times 10^{-4}$. However, continuing with missing data resulted in a increase in bias to $2 \times 10^{-4}$. Additionally, inserting missing data based on adjacent information led to a bias of $1.5 \times 10^{-4}$. During this period, the LAMOST identified 3779339 missing data points, comprising 27.4% of all missing data, specifically 16.4% among 5-minute intervals and 57.7% among 1-hour intervals of the previous K1 grille

In graph-based methods for analyzing images, graphs are created either by connecting image pixels together or by extracting features from them. A significant approach uses the dual representation, as it guarantees that nodes and cells both possess the same level of detail. Researchers have successfully applied this method to partitioning tasks for complex two-dimensional images, but its use in medicial images is limited due to computational demands and lack of prior implementation. In this study, we present the first application of edge-gated network tools for partitional semantic segmentation of medical images. We developed a novel model called the Edge-Gated Convolutional Network (EGCNN), which enhances a graph-based network by incorporating additional features to represent cell uncertainties. By training the model in two stages, we avoid excessive computational requirements and ensure consistent performance. Our results demonstrate that EGCNN achieves competitive accuracy and memory efficiency without the need for extensive preprocessing, and is particularly effective for challenging cases such as large, interconnected structures.

We address the prevalence of large-scale online databases by focusing on MongoDB and its use of document store technology. Although MongoDB is popular for its flexibility and ease of replication, its transactional implementation lacks documented details on how it ensures memory consistency. We delve into the architecture of MongoDB's distributed transactional system, outlining the relevant memory operations and their orderings. We formalize these consistency guarantees within a theoretical framework and analyze the transaction protocol for correctness. Furthermore, we evaluate the protocol's memory usage and performance efficiency.

Using the elementary symmetric function basis, we re-express the chromatic symmetric functions of Dyck paths with a bounce number of three via a combinatorial interpretation for the inverse Kostka array, showing that the coefficients are non-negative integers. Our analysis also reveals non-positivity for specific binary tree and cubic network instances. Moreover, our work provides an explanation for a previously discovered $e$-positivity property, where the coefficients of the elementary symmetric function basis are seen as bounce-separated, contributing to the broader conjecture of Reutenauer and Simion.

We propose a function called Executive Function, represented as a pair of neural network components. The first component, Exec, takes an agent's past experience into account and uses it to determine how much to invest in exploring new information. The second component, Sum, analyzes the agent's past actions and learning rate to assign a value to investing in exploration, considering a way to efficiently transform the agent's history into a meaningful reward-based decision. This proposal builds on the concept of exploring how the agent's past behavior can be transformed into a more effective strategy for making investment decisions, which is relevant to understanding executive function in the context of human experience and hindsight bias. We validate our model through experiments on artificial environments and discussions on potential applications to summarization and other relevant fields.

The primary challenge in training accurate medical image diagnostics using deep learning is ensuring the model generalizes effectively and doesn't incorporate biases present in the training data. This research focuses on developing an effective method to identify and assess inherent biases in medical image datasets. We propose a straightforward yet robust approach to detect inherent biases, evaluate their reliability, and measure their spread across different subsets of the data. We then examine two commonly used medical image datasets, monochromacity and gender bias in skin lesion analysis, to demonstrate the results of our method. Moreover, we investigate potential causes for these biases and analyze their distribution. This study is intended to set a standard for assessing data biases, which can guide researchers in evaluating med image diagnostic models' performance and inform them about potential issues arising from models learning dataset biases rather than relevant medical information.

The hidden structural characteristics of intricate systems necessitate advanced analytical techniques for comprehensive understanding. Employing networks as a case study, this research reveals essential linkages between underlying geometry and surface phenomena through the use of conjugate variables. A complex Ising model, featuring an intricate topological configuration and random interaction strengths, is investigated to demonstrate how distinct phases of ordered behavior can emerge from disordered dynamics. Furthermore, the effects of triangle-based interactions on ordered phases are examined, illustrating the applicability of network-based approaches to confined physical systems and exposing limitations of conventional mean-field theories.

A phenomenon known as solar breeze occurs at the boundary between the heliosphere and interstellar space, and its characteristics can be determined by analyzing the energy flux near the inner solar system. Data from four different spacecraft at different orbital distances reveal that electron energy flux dominates over ion energy flux near the Sun, but this changes to ion dominance as the orbit expands and crosses the 3 astronomical units mark. The relative dominance can be attributed to different processes affecting electrons and energy particles, and this has significant implications for how the heliosphere interacts with the interstellar medium and solar energy flux may serve as a remote sensing tool to retrieve solar wind parameters from external observations of the heliosphere's boundary.

Speech-emotion recognition is a deep deep learning technique that automatically determines a person's feelings from their tone via analysis of a speech pattern.  This project aims to adapt state-of-the-art speech-emotion classification models to accurately identify real-world emotions from the ORCHID dataset, which has a limited amount of information available for training.  To adapt the model effectively, a deep learning model is employed that utilizes supervised learning techniques to determine the emotions expressed in a speech sample.  However, due to limited data, the initial model tends to over-fit and produces inaccurate results.  To overcome this challenge, a novel approach is introduced that involves transferring knowledge from a large corpus of data to the limited speech-emotion classification task.  This involves adapting the extracted features for maximum entropy, which minimizes the amount of information conveyed about the target dataset.  Experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms baseline models, yielding substantial improvements in accuracy, recall, and F1 scores.

We present an investigation of the magnetic and structural changes in four-layer Aurivillius Bi5FeTi3O15 under high pressure, using a combination of nuclear forward scattering and high-pressure X-ray diffraction. At 10 K, Bi5FeTi3O15 exhibits weak long-range magnetic order with B-site sublattices following an A-type pattern and interacting in a bilayer antiferromagnetic manner along the c-axis. As pressure increases, the structural and magnetic properties of Bi5FeTi3O15 gradually become more rigid, with an associated decline in magnetic order. Bi5FeTi3O15 demonstrates better oxygen sub-lattice stability compared to its six-layer counterpart Bi6NbFe3O19 under similar high-pressure conditions.
